intelligence.essence: Possible-History Fairness-Debt Law: NayaNET shall calculate lower and upper fairness-debt bounds across all independently defensible scheduling histories, preserving both current debt and the maximum historical debt. Missing eligibility, service, or sequencing evidence shall remain explicit uncertainty. No fairness violation or compliance claim may be independently certified unless that conclusion holds across all compatible histories under the qualified scheduling contract. The desired behavior: 'I know the recovery is currently serviced, but I cannot yet prove whether it exceeded its earlier waiting bound. My current debt is zero; my possible historical peak is two to three. I will preserve that uncertainty, reconstruct the missing evidence, and certify the result only when the remaining histories justify it.' That is mathematically conservative without letting missing records manufacture guilt, erase a breach, or obscure the evidence needed to decide.
intelligence.falsifier: Current-debt-only tracking erasing a possible historical breach after service; missing intervals assumed to contain exactly one event; correlated missing rounds treated as independent choices (admitting histories inconsistent with authoritative governance, e.g. H3 around a committed withdrawal); empty compatible-history set vacuously proving compliance or violation; new evidence that expands rather than narrows the history set disguised as routine uncertainty reduction; a model that silently excludes a valid history; debt assumed to start at zero without a qualified checkpoint; states merged on debt alone while carrying different constraint contexts.

human_view.meaning: When evidence is missing, don't guess a number — compute every number the evidence still allows. Two quantities, always kept separate: what the debt could be right now, and how high it could have risen at any point. The second is the one that decides whether a deadline was ever breached — and the four-round worked example proves why it matters: three uncertain rounds, then a successful service resets debt to zero. A current-debt-only checker declares compliance. The peak-preserving calculator reports peak two-to-three: one compatible history breached, one didn't, verdict unresolved — and if reconstruction later proves the missing round eligible, the breach stands even though the system looks healthy now. The state machine is the existing canonical debt rule (unserved increments, proven service resets, ineligibility leaves it, reassignment never clears it), propagated as a set of reachable (debt, peak, context) states through every transition the evidence permits. Three safeguards are explicit: never start from zero without a qualified checkpoint, never merge states that carry different constraint futures just because the debt numbers match, and never assume a missing interval held exactly one round. Correlations are preserved — two disputed rounds around one withdrawal can't be picked independently, because a committed withdrawal that stays effective makes 'ineligible then eligible' an impossible history. Negative service evidence gets its due: the absence of a SERVICED log is not proof of no service, so the possible histories must include a reset unless a complete qualified service record excludes it. An unbounded missing interval means an infinite peak bound — which says the evidence can't cap it, not that infinite waiting happened. Every calculation ships a receipt: obligation, contract revision, starting-state evidence, interval coverage, LAW/dependency/resource evidence, service coverage, constraint-model hash, the four bounds, breach/no-breach witness histories, and the verifier's recomputation. A proven violation needs every compatible history to breach, not one failing example; a proven no-breach needs none to reach the threshold; an undetermined result keeps two witness histories — one that breaches, one that doesn't — so you know exactly which missing evidence would decide it. Twelve adversarial tests, crowned by D3: historical violation hidden by a later service must be preserved, and a current-debt-only mutant must be caught.
